questions.stem: According to the passage, who invented the geography game Worldle?
options: British data scientist Richard Mann
French video game developer Antoine Teuf
English teacher Larry Ferlazzo
Danish teacher Eva Pors
questions.evidence: French video game developer Antoine Teuf said he invented Worldle
questions.explanation_ko: 지리 게임 Worldle은 프랑스의 비디오 게임 개발자 Antoine Teuf가 만들었다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT listed as an online service teachers can use to "gamify" learning?
options: Kahoot!
Nearpod
Quizziz
Duolingo
questions.evidence: They include Kahoot!, Quizlet, Quizziz and Nearpod.
questions.explanation_ko: 본문에는 Kahoot!, Quizlet, Quizziz, Nearpod가 언급되지만 Duolingo는 언급되지 않았습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about why Richard Mann created Nerdle?
options: Wordle's popularity inspired the creation of similar word- and logic-based games for other subjects.
Nerdle was created before Wordle existed.
Math teachers dislike games similar to Wordle.
Wordle was originally designed to teach mathematics.
questions.evidence: He thought there should be a game for people who like mathematics and developed Nerdle.
questions.explanation_ko: Wordle의 인기를 보고 수학을 좋아하는 사람들을 위한 게임이 있어야겠다고 생각해 Nerdle을 만들었다는 내용에서, Wordle의 성공이 다른 과목의 비슷한 게임 제작에 영감을 주었음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author describe the "hot or cold" and "questions and answers" games in detail?
options: To give examples of language-learning games that do not require a computer
To argue that computer-based games are better
To criticize teachers who don't use technology
To explain how to build a classroom computer lab
questions.evidence: English language teacher Larry Ferlazzo asked them to share their language-learning games.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 예시들은 컴퓨터 없이도 할 수 있는 언어 학습 게임을 보여 주기 위해 소개되었습니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "gamification" mean?
options: a type of computer virus
the practice of making activities more like games to increase interest
a way of grading tests
a method of teaching without technology
questions.evidence: a learning theory called “ gamification ” to keep students’ interest
questions.explanation_ko: gamification은 활동을 게임처럼 만들어 흥미를 높이는 방식을 뜻합니다.

blanks.expression: see areas that students can improve
blanks.meaning: 학생들이 개선할 수 있는 부분을 파악하다
blanks.sentence_ko: 교사들은 결과를 살펴보고 학생들이 개선할 수 있는 부분을 파악할 수 있다.
학생들은 찾는 사람이 물건에 가까워지면 목소리를 더 크게, 멀어지면 더 작게 낸다.
그 그룹의 다른 두 학생이 이어서 1분 동안 그 역할을 넘겨받는다.
이는 학생들의 흥미를 유지하기 위한 게임화라는 학습 이론의 일부이다.

key_points: Since Wordle became popular, teachers have used it and similar games, along with an educational theory called gamification, to make learning more enjoyable.
Games like Nerdle (math) and Worldle (geography) were created because their inventors were inspired by Wordle's popularity.
Online tools like Blooket, Flippity, Kahoot!, Quizlet, Quizziz, and Nearpod let teachers turn quizzes and vocabulary practice into competitive games.
Teachers without computer access have also shared low-tech language-learning games, such as 'hot or cold' and 'questions and answers,' which help students practice vocabulary.
main_idea: Inspired partly by the popularity of Wordle, teachers are increasingly using both online and low-tech games to make learning more enjoyable and engaging for students.
restate_sentence: Creative teachers have long found games could make their classes more enjoyable for students.
